item.text:
**Bottom line**
Mostly no. In 2024, the best evidence points to loyalist filtering, selective clemency, controlled oversight, and retaliation against independent reporting. I did find a few limited counter-signals, but they look discretionary and narrow, not like a durable anti-nepotism or anti-clientelism norm.

**Evidence**
- [Iran's presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2024/06/25/world/politics/iran-election-khamenei-loyalists/) | Reuters | 2024-06-25  
  Claim: Khamenei ensured hardline views dominated the candidate field, with the Guardian Council screening 80 applicants down to six. That is strong evidence of loyalty-first appointments rather than neutral, non-favoritist selection.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.5, 7B.8

- [Iran bans ex-president Rouhani from running for elite assembly](https://theprint.in/world/iran-bans-ex-president-rouhani-from-running-for-elite-assembly/1937211/) | Reuters | 2024-01-24  
  Claim: The Guardian Council barred Rouhani from the Assembly of Experts, which can appoint or dismiss the supreme leader. That shows loyalist gatekeeping of a nominal oversight body.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.7

- [Factbox-Key facts about Iran's elections on Friday](https://theprint.in/world/factbox-key-facts-about-irans-elections-on-friday/1983652/) | Reuters | 2024-02-29  
  Claim: Assembly of Experts candidates must pass Guardian Council vetting, and the Council is itself shaped by the supreme leader’s camp. That makes the succession/oversight mechanism structurally dependent, not independent.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.7

- [IRGCs extend control over Tehran's oil exports](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/irans-revolutionary-guards-extend-control-over-tehrans-oil-exports-sources-say-3778558) | Reuters | 2024-12-18  
  Claim: Reuters reported the IRGC controlled up to half of Iran’s oil exports through shadow fleets and front companies. That is strong evidence of clientelist capture of a core state revenue stream.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.4, 7B.3

- [Journalists Ordered to Serve Five Years in Prison in Iran](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/24/journalists-ordered-serve-five-years-prison-iran) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-24  
  Claim: The judiciary enforced prison sentences against journalists for reporting on Mahsa Amini’s death and framed the case as propaganda against the state. That is direct punishment of independent information and a warning to other reporters.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.7, 7B.8, 7B.6

- [Two years after Woman, Life, Freedom, impunity for crimes reigns supreme](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11  
  Claim: Amnesty said there were no effective, impartial investigations into killings, torture, sexual violence, or disappearances, and that families seeking truth faced harassment and arbitrary detention. That shows concealment and retaliation, not accountability.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.7, 7B.8, 7B.6

- [Iran barred many experienced inspectors, IAEA board demanded reversal](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaea-board-passes-resolution-against-iran-on-cooperation-inspectors-3472087) | Reuters | 2024-06-05  
  Claim: Iran had barred many of the IAEA’s top enrichment experts, and the board demanded reversal. This is strong evidence against openness to independent scrutiny in a sensitive domain.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7

- [Pezeshkian Cabinet: Profiles](https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2024/aug/22/pezeshkian-cabinet-profiles) | The Iran Primer / USIP | 2024-08-22  
  Claim: The cabinet included reformists, hardliners, technocrats, and academics, and Pezeshkian had Khamenei, IRGC, and security-agency approval before submitting it. This is the best limited counter-signal for competence-based staffing, but it still looks compromise-driven inside a loyalist system.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.5, 7B.8

- [Ayatollah Khamenei pardons, commutes sentences of over 2,000 prisoners](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2024/04/06/723171/-Supreme-Leader-Ayatollah-Khamenei-pardons-commutes-sentences-of-over-2%2C000-Iranian-inmates) | Press TV | 2024-04-06  
  Claim: Khamenei used his constitutional clemency power for 2,127 inmates, including some security-related cases and minors. This is a limited positive sign, but it is discretionary and selective rather than a rule-based rejection of favoritism.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.7, 7B.8

- [Iran reduces sentence of jailed journalists after clearing them of collaborating with US](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/iran-reduces-sentence-of-jailed-journalists-after-clearing-them-of-collaborating-with-us-3660786) | Reuters | 2024-10-13  
  Claim: A court dropped one charge and reduced the journalists’ sentences, which is the closest corrective signal I found. But they were still punished for reporting on Amini’s death, so this was only partial relief.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.7, 7B.6

- [Iran will not impede IAEA access, head of its atomic organisation says](https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/) | Reuters | 2024-12-14  
  Claim: Iran said it would not obstruct IAEA access and would operate within safeguards. This is a narrow late-year procedural openness signal, but not evidence of broad anti-clientelism or honesty about tradeoffs.  
  IDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6

**Search gap**
I did not find reliable 2024 public reporting directly documenting Khamenei family members receiving named contracts, explicit bribes, or clearly kin-based procurement favoritism. The public record is much stronger on indirect patronage and loyalist control than on a direct, documentable nepotism trail.
